verification_note: Indirect abstract/citing-paper support: Auger et al. (2003), Crop Protection 22:1039-1044, reports tebufenpyrad resistance ratios of 16.8-39.8 in P. ulmi from southern French apple orchards, relative to the more susceptible reference population. This is the study range, not an independently verified Vaucluse-specific value. Yaman et al. (2016), J. Agricultural Sciences 22:249-260, p.259 (PDF p.11), explicitly cites Auger et al. and repeats this tebufenpyrad range. Country, field orchard origin and 2003 publication supported. Original full PDF not obtained. DOI:10.1016/S0261-2194(03)00136-4. Citing PDF: https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/1569165.

Indirect original-abstract support: Gorman, Hewitt, Denholm & Devine report marked fenbutatin oxide resistance in a collected UK glasshouse T. urticae population. No numerical resistance ratio or Warwickshire allocation is given in the accessible abstract. Year yes accepts first online publication on 10 December 2001. The formal journal citation is Gorman et al. (2002), Pest Management Science 58(2):123-130, not a 2001 journal issue. Original full PDF not obtained; R left blank. DOI:10.1002/ps.427; PMID:11852636. Publisher: https://scijournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/ps.427.

Original publisher abstract confirms high hexythiazox cross-resistance in T. urticae from Queensland glasshouse roses after intensive commercial clofentezine use. Thus species, Australia, glasshouse origin and 1993 publication are supported indirectly. The >2500-fold figure belongs to clofentezine and must not be assigned to hexythiazox; no hexythiazox-specific fold was verified, so R is blank. Citation correction: the first author is Grant Herron (Herron, G.), not Grant, H. Correct citation: Herron, Edge & Rophail (1993), Exp. Appl. Acarol. 17:433-440. Original full PDF not obtained. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00120501.

Indirect original-abstract verification: Hu et al. (2010), Pest Management Science 66:1025-1030, sampled six P. citri populations from Chinese citrus orchards. It explicitly reports resistance to all tested acaricides in Pinghe and identifies pyridaben resistance in Jianning. Pyridaben LC50 values across samples were 48.90-609.91 mg/L; these are concentrations, not resistance ratios. No compound-specific RR was verified from the accessible abstract, so R is blank. Country China, field origin and 2010 publication supported. Original full PDF not obtained. DOI:10.1002/ps.1978; PMID:20540074.

Indirect original-abstract verification: Hu et al. (2010), Pest Management Science 66:1025-1030, explicitly reports cross-resistance to spirotetramat in the spirodiclofen-resistant Pinghe and Fuzhou P. citri populations collected from Chinese citrus orchards in 2009. The 50- and 90.8-fold values in that abstract are for spirodiclofen, not spirotetramat. Spirotetramat resistance is supported, but its own numerical RR was not verified; R is blank. Species, China, field sampling and 2010 publication supported. Original full PDF not obtained. DOI:10.1002/ps.1978; PMID:20540074.

Liu et al. (2020), Pesticide Biochemistry and Physiology 163:31-38, confirms cyflumetofen resistance in T. cinnabarinus strains CyR and YN-CyR (original abstract; PMID:31973868). Field resistance before selection is not established. Cross-reference: Transcriptome analysis revealed that multiple genes were related to the cyflumetofen resistance of T. cinnabarinus (2021), 173:104799, describes the Yunnan 2014 field-derived YS strain as relatively susceptible, maintained without acaricides, then selected to produce YN-CyR. Thus Q=no concerns laboratory generation of resistance, despite field ancestry. The database's 'after field-evolved resistance' wording needs recheck. No fold from the later selection study is transferred to this 2020 case. Original PDF not obtained. DOIs:10.1016/j.pestbp.2019.10.001 and 10.1016/j.pestbp.2021.104799.

Indirect support: the original abstract describes T. urticae collected from ten rose houses, with dicofol resistance persisting despite seven years without dicofol use. Khajehali (2010), Biochemical and molecular mechanisms of acaricide resistance in T. urticae, Ghent University PhD thesis, printed p.23 (PDF p.39), explicitly links Overmeer et al. (1975) to Aalsmeer, Netherlands; the full reference is on printed p.155 (PDF p.171). Correct authors include W. Helle, omitted from the source citation. Publication year is 1975; the 2011 date is archive digitisation. No numerical RR verified; R blank. Original 1975 PDF not obtained. DOI:10.1111/j.1570-7458.1975.tb00387.x. Citing thesis: https://backoffice.biblio.ugent.be/download/1077046/1077058.

Original Pan et al. (2020) PDF checked. Table 1, p.919, identifies Anyue, Sichuan, China, on Citrus limon. Methods confirm orchard-collected P. citri. Table 2, p.920, gives Anyue fenpropathrin RR=52.27 in 2017 and 47.27 in 2018, versus S-strain LC50=0.266 mg/L; corresponding field LC50 values are 13.91 and 12.57 mg/L. R contains this Anyue-specific range. These table values meet the paper's high-resistance class (40-60), despite the abstract's broad low/moderate summary for southwestern populations. Publication year 2020 is the issue year; advance access was 10 December 2019. DOI:10.1093/jee/toz335. PDF: https://www1.montpellier.inrae.fr/CBGP/spmweb/pdf/Authors_P/Pan_et_al_2020.pdf.

Indirect original-abstract verification: Pan et al. (2023), Pest Management Science 79:996-1004, monitored ten Chinese P. citri populations during 2014-2021. Field populations from Yuxi, Anyue, Nanning and Ganzhou exceeded 1000-fold pyridaben resistance relative to Lab_S. R records that reported lower bound for field populations. The paper also includes Pyr_R and segregated laboratory strains for fitness tests; those results are separate from the field monitoring. Species, China, field sampling and 2023 issue year are supported (online publication in 2022). The exact history of the particular Pyr_R laboratory line was not verified from full text. Original full PDF not obtained. DOI:10.1002/ps.7270; PMID:36318043.

Original accepted manuscript checked: Rameshgar et al. (2019), Crop Protection 125:104903. Methods section 2.1 (PDF p.5) confirms collection of P. ulmi from Iranian commercial apple orchards during 2016-2017. Table 2 (PDF p.20) reports Mahabad abamectin RR=46.13 (95% CI 25.70-82.79), LC50=5.50 mg a.i./L, versus PSR-TK. R uses the published population-specific ratio rather than the abstract's overall 11-46 range or a new calculation from rounded LC50 values. Year 2019 supported. Correct final author's spelling: Van Leeuwen. DOI:10.1016/j.cropro.2019.104903. Accepted manuscript: https://biblio.ugent.be/publication/8638535/file/8643841.pdf.

Indirect original-abstract support: Roy et al. (2018), International Journal of Acarology 44(1):41-45, DOI:10.1080/01647954.2017.1402954. The abstract reproduced on coauthor Bithika Phukan's public profile describes eight field tea populations in Assam, India, and high/very high resistance to ethion and dicofol. It gives a joint 13.58-134.27-fold range for the two acaricides without separating dicofol's range. R is blank to avoid assigning the combined range to dicofol alone. Species, India/Assam, field origin and 2018 issue year supported; online first was 27 November 2017. Original full PDF not obtained. Abstract: https://independent.academia.edu/BithikaPhukan. Metadata verified against publisher-deposited Crossref record.

Indirect abstract/section support: Sato et al. (2016), Crop Protection 89:278-283, evaluated 23 Brazilian field populations, finding 0-81.5% resistant mites. Those are resistance frequencies, not fold ratios. Its RR50=121 was obtained after 20 laboratory selection cycles in a mixture originating from four chrysanthemum-field populations; it is not an Artur Nogueira field-population RR. Species, Brazil, year and field-monitoring component supported. The Artur Nogueira-specific monitoring row was not recovered, so the exact case remains partly verified and R is blank. Original full PDF not obtained. DOI:10.1016/j.cropro.2016.08.003. Abstract: https://bv.fapesp.br/pt/publicacao/125908/spiromesifen-resistance-in-tetranychus-urticae-acari-tetra/.

Original Sato et al. (2004) PDF checked. Methods, p.294: source T. urticae collected in September 1999 from a commercial strawberry field in Atibaia, Sao Paulo, Brazil. Table 3, p.298, reports pyridaben RR50=53.1 and RR95=88.9 for the fenpyroximate-selected R strain versus the susceptibility-selected S strain. Footnotes specify five resistance selections and three susceptibility selections. R records the published RR50=53.1, explicitly a laboratory cross-resistance result, not an unselected field pyridaben ratio. Q=no reflects that distinction; field ancestry is confirmed. The stated 'after field-evolved resistance' to pyridaben is not established by this experiment. DOI:10.1303/aez.2004.293. Original PDF: https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/aez/39/2/39_2_293/_pdf/-char/en.

Original Suh et al. (2006) text examined online: field/glasshouse sampling and testing within about two generations are described on p.153; Table 1, p.157, reports fenpyroximate ratios by population number. The figure-to-Gumi mapping was not verified, so no other population's fold is assigned. Korean field resistance is supported; this named case needs mapping recheck. DOI:10.1007/s10493-006-0009-z. Text: https://www.academia.edu/67318610. Original PDF not downloaded.

Original Suh et al. (2006) text examined online. Methods p.153 confirms Korean field/glasshouse collections; Table 2, p.158, gives pyridaben RR by population number against strain S. The Cheongju-to-population-number mapping was not verified. R is blank; the table-wide range is not substituted for Cheongju's fold. DOI:10.1007/s10493-006-0009-z. Text: https://www.academia.edu/67318610. Original PDF not downloaded.

Original Suh et al. (2006) text examined online. Methods p.153 confirms Korean field/glasshouse collections; Table 2, p.158, reports numbered populations' pyridaben resistance. Yeongcheon's corresponding population number was not independently verified. R is blank rather than borrowing another population's ratio. Species, country, year and field origin supported; locality mapping remains open. DOI:10.1007/s10493-006-0009-z. Text: https://www.academia.edu/67318610. Original PDF not downloaded.

Indirect original-abstract support: Van Leeuwen, Van Pottelberge & Tirry (2005), Pest Management Science 61:499-507, explicitly reports strong bifenthrin resistance in field-collected MR-VL versus LS-VL. De Beer et al. (2022), DOI:10.1016/j.ibmb.2022.103757, Methods section 2.1, accepted PDF p.6 (printed p.4, lines 118-120), identifies MR-VL as originally collected in a Ghent University greenhouse and cites the 2005 study, supporting Belgium and glasshouse origin. No bifenthrin RR was verified; R is blank. Original 2005 full PDF not obtained. DOI:10.1002/ps.1001; PMID:15657956. Citing PDF: https://biblio.ugent.be/publication/8745795/file/8745802.pdf.

Indirect original-abstract support: Van Leeuwen, Van Pottelberge & Tirry (2005), Pest Management Science 61:499-507, explicitly reports strong dicofol resistance in field-collected MR-VL versus LS-VL. De Beer et al. (2022), DOI:10.1016/j.ibmb.2022.103757, Methods section 2.1, accepted PDF p.6 (printed p.4, lines 118-120), confirms MR-VL originated in a Ghent University greenhouse and cites the 2005 paper. Species, Belgium, glasshouse origin and 2005 year supported. No dicofol-specific RR was verified; R is blank. Original 2005 full PDF not obtained. DOI:10.1002/ps.1001; PMID:15657956. Original Vassiliou & Kitsis (2013) PDF text inspected online. Table 1 identifies Arediou/Nicosia, Cyprus, greenhouse roses, collected 24 February 2010. Table 2 and Abamectin Resistance Status give AREDIOU LC50=83.29 mg a.i./L and RR=3822 (95% CI 3158-4626) versus the German susceptible GSS strain. These are the Arediou-specific values, not a study-wide maximum assigned without a locality check. Methods confirm field/glasshouse collection and rearing without selection before bioassay. Journal of Economic Entomology 106:1848-1854 (2013). DOI:10.1603/EC12369. Online original PDF: https://academic.oup.com/jee/article-pdf/106/4/1848/19292044/jee106-1848.pdf. Local download was blocked.

Indirect original-abstract verification: Xu et al. (2018), Pesticide Biochemistry and Physiology 150:89-96, used a leaf-dip assay on seven Chinese field populations of T. urticae and reports low/moderate resistance to cyenopyrafen among these populations. Species, tested compound, China, field origin and 2018 publication are supported. The Harbin-specific table row and numerical fold were not obtained; R is blank rather than using a value for another population or another acaricide. The missing DOI is 10.1016/j.pestbp.2018.07.008. PMID:30195393. Original full PDF not obtained. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30195393/.

Indirect original-abstract verification: Xu et al. (2021), Pest Management Science 77:1204-1213, explicitly studies abamectin-resistant field population NB-ZJ in China, alongside SY-BJ and Lab-SS. The 2.95-fold PBO and 3.55-fold TPP figures for NB-ZJ are synergistic ratios, not abamectin resistance ratios; neither is entered in R. A NB-ZJ-specific RR was not verified. The abstract supports species, compound resistance, China and field origin. The 2021 issue year is correct, with first online publication in 2020. Ningbo allocation is not independently established by the target abstract. Original full PDF not obtained. DOI:10.1002/ps.6130; PMID:33034948. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33034948/.
